'''Ghulam Dastagir Alam Qasmi''' ({{langx|ur|غلام دستگیر عالم قاسمی}}; popularly known as '''G.D. Alam'''; {{small|[[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]], [[Hilal-e-Imtiaz|''HI'']]}}; 1937 – 5 December 2000), was a Pakistani [[theoretical physicist]] and professor of mathematics at the [[Quaid-e-Azam University]]. Alam is best known for conceiving and embarking on research on the [[gas centrifuge]] during Pakistan's integrated [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|atomic bomb project]] in the 1970s, and he also conceived the research on [[charge density]], nuclear fission, and [[gamma-ray bursts]] throughout his career.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Allam |first1=GD |last2=Rashid |first2=Khalid |last3=Ahmad |first3=Maqsood |last4=Qureshi |first4=I.E. |last5=Ali |first5=Anwar |last6=Khan |first6=Naeem Ahmad |last7=Bhatti |first7=Nasim |last8=Horsh |first8=F. |title=GAMMA RAY TRANSITIONS IN DE-EXCITATION OF CF-252 SPONTANEOUS FISSION FRAGMENTS |url=https://inis.iaea.org/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/16/072/16072330.pdf |website=www.inis.iaea.org |publisher=IAEA and PINSTECH |access-date=9 August 2020 |location=Nilore, Islamabad |pages=28 |language=en-us |date=1 November 1983 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Vandenbosch |first1=Robert |title=Nuclear Fission |date=2012 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-323-15052-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RCeaisb73M0C&q=GD%20Alam |access-date=9 August 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

After the atomic bomb project, Alam joined the Department of Mathematics at the Quaid-e-Azam University (QAU) as well as serving as [[Visiting professor|visiting faculty]] at the [[Institute of Physics]], and co-authored papers on [[Calculus of variations|variation calculus]] and [[Nuclear isomer|fission isomer]]. He was one of the notable theoretical physicists at the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) and QAU. At one point, his fellow theorist, [[Munir Ahmad Khan]], called Alam "the problem solving brain of the PAEC".{{rp|155}}<ref name="Stanford University Press">{{cite book|last=Khan|first=Feroz Hassan|title=Eating grass : the making of the Pakistani bomb|publisher=Stanford University Press|location=Stanford, California|isbn=978-0804776011|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC&q=eating+grass+the+making+of+the+pakistani+bomb|access-date=28 February 2013|chapter=Cascade to Enriching|date=2012-11-07}}</ref>

==Biography==

Alam was educated at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] in [[Lahore]] where he studied in 1951 and graduated with [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) in [[Mathematics]] in 1955 under the supervision of [[Abdus Salam]]–a theoretical physicist.<ref name="MSc Thesis by GD Alam, 1957"/> He then went to attend the physics program at the [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] where he graduated with [[Master of Science]] (MSc) in [[Physics]] in 1957, supervised under Dr. [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|Rafi Muhammad]]– a nuclear physicist.<ref name="MSc Thesis by GD Alam, 1957"/>

His thesis titled: ''The Emission of Electromagnetic Radiations from metals by high energy particles'', had contained investigations on electromagnetic radiation emitted from the heavy metals by bombarding the elementary particles.<ref name="MSc Thesis by GD Alam, 1957">{{cite web |last1=Qasmi |first1=GD Allam |title=The Emission of Electromagnetic Radiations from metals by high energy particles. |url=https://defence.pk/pdf/ |website=www.defence.pk/pdf/ |publisher=NM Butt |access-date=8 August 2020 |location=Islamabad |language=en-us |archive-date=11 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311200918/https://defence.pk/pdf/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>N. M. Butt, “Nuclear Radiation Education and Nuclear Science and Technology in Pakistan,” paper presented to the 2nd International Congress on Radiation Education in Debrecen, Hungary</ref>

In 1964, Alam joined the doctoral program in physics at the [[University College London]] (UCL) under the [[Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan|Colombo Plan Scholarship]], initially joining the doctoral group led by British physicist, [[John Hasted|John B. Hasted]].<ref name="PhD Thesis by GD Alam, 1967">{{cite web |last1=Alam |first1=GD |title=Electron Capture by Multiply Charged Ions |url=https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1572456/1/Alam.Qasmi_thesis.pdf |website=www.discovery.ucl.ac.uk |publisher=University College London Press |access-date=8 August 2020 |location=London, Eng. UK |pages=142 |language=en-uk |date=1 February 1967 }}</ref> He learned the course on [[atomic physics]] under [[Harrie Massey]] and worked on experimental physics under J.B. Hasted.{{rp|137}}<ref name="PhD Thesis by GD Alam, 1967"/> In 1967, he submitted his doctoral thesis supervised by Dr. J.B. Hasted which he defended successfully and graduated with [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in theoretical physics.{{rp|11–142}}<ref name="PhD Thesis by GD Alam, 1967"/> His doctoral thesis, titled: ''Electron Capture by Multiply Charged Ions'', provided scientific investigations on [[Charge-exchange ionization|charge-crossing]] involving potential [[Avoided crossing|curve crossing]], a concept in [[quantum mechanics]].{{rp|11–142}}<ref name="PhD Thesis by GD Alam, 1967"/>

In 1967, he published another thesis jointly written by J.B. Hasted and [[Diethard Böhme|D.K. Bohme]] on physics of atomic collision and potential energy curves— their work was supported and funded by the [[United States Department of Defense]].<ref name="United States. Dept. of Defense">{{cite web|last=W. Benjamin., 1967|first=United States. Dept. of Defense|title=Charge Transfer Involving Curve Crossin|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=K4_vAAAAMAAJ&q=gd+alam+university+of+london|work=W. Benjamin., 1967|publisher=United States. Dept. of Defense|access-date=27 December 2011|year=1967}}</ref>

While in the [[United Kingdom]], Alam continued publishing and working on the atomic physics and atomic collisions, collaborating with many other of his British colleagues.<ref name="Academic Press Inc.">{{cite book|last=Bates|first=David Robert|title=Advances in Atomic and Molecular Physics|year=1967|publisher=Academic Press Inc.|location=Uk. Usa|isbn=9780080564647|pages=243–247|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PC84mcV0uzwC&q=alam&pg=PA443}}</ref> However, Alam lost interests in atomic physics and became interested in [[computer programming]] and mathematics.{{rp|80; 425}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" /> In 1970, he published a paper on gamma rays and performed an experiment on isomers, proposing and later proving mathematically that, in the isomer state, the average [[kinetic energy]] associated with the decay process of Isomer state is about the same in the [[ground state]] of fission.<ref name="Library of Congress/Springer Limited (Germany)">{{cite book|last=Hooshyar |first=M. Ali |author2=Irwin Reichstein|author3= F. B. Malik|title=Nuclear Fission and Cluster Radioactivity: An Energy-Density Functional Approach |year=2005 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin; New York |isbn=3-540-23302-4 |pages=136–151 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Sg9Bjx9Pr8AC&q=alam&pg=PA151}}</ref>

==Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission==
===1971 war, atomic bomb program, and centrifuge technology===
{{Main|Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|Gas centrifuge|Supercomputing in Pakistan}}
[[File:Gas centrifuge nrc.png|thumb|left|170px|{{small|A schematic of gas centrifuge employed in the United States, copyright by U.S. [[Nuclear Regulatory Commission|NRC]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/fact-sheets/enrichment.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=8 August 2020 |archive-date=3 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160503222302/http://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/fact-sheets/enrichment.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1970s, Alam had conceived a concept of gas centrifuge independent of A.Q. Khan's Urenco-based designs.{{rp|57}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/>}}]]
In 1958, Alam joined the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] as a researcher, and was directed to join the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] (PINSTECH), the national laboratory site in Nilore, in 1970.{{rp|8}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/> During the [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1971|war with India]] in 1971, Alam became interested in computing and mathematics, briefly writing a computer program while working in problems relating to logic and the mathematics.{{rp|8}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" /> Alam was instrumental in establishing the computer department at the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology before moving to join the Physics Division.{{rp|53}}<ref name="Printwise publications">{{cite book|last=Shahid-Ur Rehman|title=Long Road to Chagai: §The Gas centrifuge controversy|year=1999|publisher=Printwise publications|location=Pakistan, UK|isbn=978-969-8500-00-9|pages=8, 53–60|chapter=The Gas-centriguce controversy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sNMgAQAAIAAJ&q=Khokhar}}</ref>

Alam originally was not part of the team that was investigating the uranium enrichment under [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Bashiruddin Mahmood]] in 1974 and had not seen a [[gas centrifuge]] albeit of rudimentary knowledge from the work done by [[Jesse Beams]], an American, in 1940s.{{rp|53–54}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/> In 1974–76, Alam directed a separate [[electromagnetic separation]] program at the Airport Development Works setup at the [[Chaklala airbase|Chaklala Air Force Base]] and begin working on the applications of [[magnetism]] and [[magnetic bearing]].{{rp|143}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" /> Eventually other physicists such as Fakhr Hashmi, Javed Arshad Mirza, Eqbal Ahmad Khokhar, and [[Anwar Ali (physicist)|Anwar Ali]] joined his Airport Development Works facility— thus forming the centrifuge program under Alam.{{rp|143–144}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" />

In 1976, Alam was asked to review the components and the blueprints of a gas centrifuge brought by [[Abdul Qadeer Khan]] for analysis, which he later identified as incorrect and incomplete to the PAEC.{{rp|146-146}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" /> During this time, he held discussion with Abdul Qadeer Khan on copper metallurgy which was nascent to his development of centrifuge at the Airport Development Works facility.{{rp|146}}<ref name="Stanford University Press" /> Meanwhile, Alam accepted and joined the faculty of mathematics at the [[Quaid-e-Azam University]] and met with [[Tasneem M. Shah|Tasneem Shah]], an Oxford University PhD graduate in mathematics, degelating Shah to join the centrifuge program.{{rp|56–57}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/> Alam and Shah performed mathematical calculations for linearly [[Approximation error|approximating]] the reasonable [[Relative change and difference|percent error]] for the actual value of military-grade uranium that proved the Abdul Qadeer Khan's estimation required to enriched the uranium.{{rp|57}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/>

In April 1976, Alam succeeded in designing a gas centrifuge and succeeded in rotating the first centrifuge to 30,000 [[Revolutions per minute|rpm]] by perfectly balancing and [[Rotation around a fixed axis|rotating around fixed axis]] of the centrifuge— Alam and his team was immediately dispatched at the [[Khan Research Laboratories]] under Abdul Qadeer Khan.{{rp|57}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/> At KRL, Alam and Shah worked on solving differential equation problems relating the gas centrifuges, and designed a first generation of centrifuges, known as ''P1'', that succeeded in separating the U<sup>234</sup>, U<sup>235</sup>, and U<sup>238</sup> isotopes from raw [[natural uranium]] under supervision of Shah, Alam, and Qadeer Khan.{{rp|58–59}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/> Commenting on the success, Alam famously quoted: "Boys, we have achieved enrichment in Pakistan."{{rp|148–149}}<ref name="Stanford University Press"/> Following this success, Alam and other colleagues signed and quickly published a paper on the differential methods of the centrifuges in 1978–79.{{rp|150–151}}<ref name="Stanford University Press"/>

Alam remained associated with the centrifuge program and was its design director until 1981 when he developed intellectual differences with Abdul Qadeer Khan in 1981.{{rp|431}}<ref name="Stanford University Press"/> He was confided by Abdul Qadeer Khan about selling the centrifuge technology to unknown Arab country, which he vehemently opposed the idea on the ground that India (a competitor in that field) might be benefited from that technology.<ref>Alam, G.D., ''Dr. Qadeer Was Ready to Secretly Sell Nuclear Technology to an Arab Country: Dr. G.D. Alam'', interview in ''Assas-o-Lashkar'' (Urdu), June 12, 1998</ref>{{rp|431}}<ref name="Stanford University Press"/> After this incident, Alam was transferred to PAEC where he remained associated with the electromagnetic separation program under Dr. [[Shaukat Hameed Khan]], and decided to work on the [[partial differential equations]].{{rp|59}}<ref name="Printwise publications"/>

Alam went to join the [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] and briefly taught courses on calculus, and published a computer model on HIV rate of infection along with American scientists.{{rp|389}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Deep |first1=Kusum |last2=Bansal |first2=Jagdish Chand |last3=Das |first3=Kedar Nath |last4=Lal |first4=Arvind Kumar |last5=Garg |first5=Harish |last6=Nagar |first6=Atulya K. |last7=Pant |first7=Millie |title=Proceedings of Sixth International Conference on Soft Computing for Problem Solving: SocProS 2016, Volume 2 |date=2017 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-981-10-3325-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4amoDgAAQBAJ&dq=GD+Alam+mathematics&pg=PA389 |access-date=8 August 2020 |language=en}}</ref> At the Department of Mathematics, Alam pioneered a paper in [[Gamma-ray burst]]s using [[Mathematical descriptions of physical laws|mathematical descriptions]] to analyse the energy released by the gamma rays.<ref name="Institution of Electrical">{{cite web|last=Alam|first=Ghulam Dastigar|title=Gamma Ray Transitions in the de-excitation Californium-253 spontenous fission pragments|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bfVWAAAAMAAJ&q=gd+alam|work=Dr. Ghulam Dastigar Alam, Department of Mathematics, Quaid-e-Azam University|publisher=Institution of Electrical|access-date=27 December 2011|year=1997}}</ref> Alam died on 5 December 2000 in his residence in Islamabad.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}
